parsed.explanation: No criminalisation of trans expression or same-sex conduct; gender identity and expression have been protected in anti-discrimination law since 2005 and, since 2014, that statute covers goods and services, health and education — genuinely visitor-relevant (hotels, clinics, transport). Social acceptance is documented and strong (marriage equality 2017, six-figure Pride, decades of organised community life). Police record hate-crime motives and a first conversion-practices prosecution succeeded. Offsetting negatives are moderate: rising recorded hate-crime counts (raw suspicions, no hate-crime offence in the code), LGBT-wide violence data with no trans-specific rate, and unresolved visitor-facing questions — border/gender-marker handling, airport screening, facility access, custody placement — plus a dated, resident-focused care-access shortfall. Open questions and resident-facing gaps carry light weight under the rubric; the documented positives are acceptance plus a working service-equality regime, not proof of enforcement outcomes for trans travellers. Hence above 0.65 anchors, short of 0.85.
